title: Replying to @its.raining.ben Show number 1 in my journey to see 7 sho...
transcript: hi, I'm Ben, and I'm seeing 7 shows in 7 days. and first up is Mike Perbiglia, The Old Man and the Pool. the show is playing at Lincoln Center Theater, which is one of my absolute favorite places to see a show. I just love walking through Lincoln Center Plaza on the way to the show, it just has this, like, magical vibe to it. it's gorgeous. you get to walk by the Metropolitan Opera House and then you walk to the theater and another thing you'll notice, which I love is the Lincoln Center will order these custom neon signs for each of their shows. and I just, I love that I think it's just such a cool, unique thing that Lincoln Center does. it looks so cool. no other theater does it. it's awesome. another unique thing about the Vivian Beaumont Theater specifically is that it's a thrust stage, so you'll notice the audience is in a semi circle around the stage, and even though the theater holds over a thousand people. it still feels really intimate because of the way the seats are arranged, which makes it the perfect venue for a show like this. I actually was not very familiar with Mike Barbiglia before I saw the show. I have a couple friends who are really big fans of his and recommended that I see it. this was my first time seeing any of his shows, and I have to say I really enjoyed myself. I thought it was incredibly funny. it might be the hardest I've laughed in a theater all year. but there were also other moments that were incredibly touching and somber and had you questioning mortality. and the fact that he is able to balance those 2 seemingly contradictory things into one show is, I think, a testament to what a great storyteller, he is. I definitely came out of the show. as a huge Microbiglia fan, I can't wait to watch the other things that he's done. and I definitely recommend checking it out before it closes in January, if you can. and I'll see you tomorrow for show too.
